info.name: ThunderID - Role B2B Sharing Demo
info.description: End-to-end demo of the Role sharing framework: create a role, share it to a Root organization unit, reshare into its subtree (including OUs created afterward and exclusion policies), reshare directly in a single call when A already sits at the top of its own subtree, reach outside an owner's own subtree via a two-step push-to-own-root path, delegate one hop at a time through a multi-level chain and verify that chain's integrity under exclusion, control per-assignee-type, grant-scoped, scope-down-only editability, prove sharee organizations can own roles of their own alongside shared ones, exercise the write-path authorization checks, confirm revocation cascades cleanly, and prove a shared role's assignment is honored by real client_credentials token issuance (RBAC). See api/role.yaml for the full REST API reference.

item.name: 00 - Setup

request.description: Obtains a system-scoped management token via client_credentials, authenticating with HTTP Basic auth (client_id/client_secret in the Authorization header, not the body) and a resource indicator. Fill in clientId/clientSecret in the environment first. (This is unrelated to the app-level client_credentials token obtained later in '08 - RBAC' — that one represents a business application, this one represents this Postman collection's own admin access.)

item.name: Set System Resource Server as Default

request.description: systemResourceServerId is the bootstrap-fixed 'System' resource server. Making it the deployment default means a client_credentials token request that omits the resource indicator resolves here. This is a deliberate, lasting deployment setting, not a throwaway demo prop, so it is not undone in '15 - Cleanup'.

Looks up the bootstrap-fixed 'System' resource server's own top-level resources to resolve the 'system' resource's id dynamically, rather than assuming the deterministic <systemResourceServerId>_system id shape.

Nesting a 'Roles' resource under the 'system' resource (systemResourceId, resolved via the preceding request) via parent, rather than a top-level resource, is what derives the permission string system:roles (parent resource's own permission + delimiter + this resource's handle) instead of a flat 'roles'.
Nesting a 'View' resource under the 'Roles' resource (systemRolesResourceId) via parent derives the permission string system:roles:view, the read-only counterpart to system:roles.

An application's own inboundAuthConfig.scopes only lists what it may request; the client_credentials grant still filters the issued token's scope through the same RBAC/role-assignment check as any other permission, so system:roles is only ever actually granted via a real role assignment like this one.
Carries the read-only system:roles:view permission; assigned to m2m applications (see '12') that should only ever list/read role data, never create, update, or delete it.

User type schemas are organization-unit-scoped, so a minimal one is created here directly in B-sub1, letting '06 - Editability Control' create and use a real user instead of requiring one to already exist in the deployment.
A real user in B-sub1, so the assignments.user editability demo in '06 - Editability Control' assigns an actual principal rather than an unverifiable placeholder ID.

This reuses the B's own role from '02' (a role B owns, and is itself a Root) to share directly to B-sub1 in a single call.

item.name: 10 - Cross-Tree Delegation via Push-to-Own-Root
item.description: A non-root owner reaching outside its own subtree (here, B-sub1's own role reaching its sibling, B-sub1b) must still go through two steps: Share to its own Root first (a deliberate step out of B-sub1's immediate subtree), then that Root reshares within its tree. This is the two-step path that remains necessary even after single-call owner distribution (folder 09) was introduced.

Lifting this restriction requires enabling resource_sharing.allow_child_ou_cross_tree_sharing in deployment.yaml and restarting the server — not something this collection can demonstrate live, so this folder only exercises the default-restricted path.

item.name: 11 - Chained Delegation and Chain Integrity
item.description: Covers two related rules on a fresh, throwaway role and organization unit: (1) an explicit reshare target must be the resharing organization unit's own direct child — reaching a grandchild (B-sub2b, created here under B-sub1) selectively requires B-sub1 to reshare again in its own, independent call; B cannot skip that level. (2) visibility must chain unbroken — excluding B-sub1 from an allChildren reshare also cuts off B-sub2b, its grandchild, even though nothing names B-sub2b directly in the exclusion list, while B-sub1b (not excluded) is unaffected.
